items.streamTitle: Conflict-misinformation ensemble reported high scores on four benchmarks
items.streamSummary: An ensemble using text, imagery and affective features reported 94.66%–98.23% accuracy across four misinformation datasets. Results were benchmark-based and do not establish live conflict performance.
items.attribution: Muhammad et al. — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: Researchers proposed testing whether agreeable AI weakens tolerance for criticism
items.streamSummary: A new Perspective argues that overly agreeable AI may undermine learners' tolerance for corrective feedback. It defines ways to test the claim but reports no new empirical evidence of harm.
items.attribution: Chen et al. — npj Digital Medicine (Perspective)

items.streamTitle: US evidence-rule advisers confronted deepfakes but reported few actual challenges
items.streamSummary: At an October 15 US judicial panel, experts warned of increasingly convincing deepfakes, while only 15 of 931 surveyed judges had seen related challenges. A subcommittee will study the issue; no rule was adopted.
items.attribution: Reuters — Nate Raymond, original reporting from US Judicial Conference meeting

items.streamTitle: Safety benchmarks changed when superficial agent-context cues were altered
items.streamSummary: An arXiv audit found large shifts in agent-safety scores under domain holdouts and alternative weighting. Small input edits affected one tested guard but not all models, underscoring evaluation fragility.
items.attribution: Demirkiran and Ernstberger — arXiv preprint (Shortcut Sensitivity)

items.streamTitle: Starlink disruptions exposed battlefield dependence on external connectivity
items.streamSummary: Reuters frontline reporting on October 16 recorded Ukrainian soldiers' accounts of disrupted command links and slower connectivity. Service recovery was incomplete, and exact downstream operational losses remain uncertain.
items.attribution: Reuters — original reporting by Sergiy Chalyi, October 16

items.streamTitle: Religious-positive posts drew higher engagement in a populist leader's X feed
items.streamSummary: Analysis of 3,967 posts by Yogi Adityanath found higher engagement for religious-affect messages. Qualitative interpretation suggests identity-boundary work without explicit hostility, but causal persuasion was not tested.
items.attribution: Peng — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: AI-supported children's drawings yielded more narrative actions, not proven learning
items.streamSummary: An exploratory 24-case classroom analysis found more observation time and narrative actions in a later AI-supported activity. Several language measures were null, and fixed session order prevents causal attribution.
items.attribution: Li et al. — Scientific Reports (Botune)

items.streamTitle: NATO expanded counter-drone interoperability experiments across defense cells
items.streamSummary: NATO ACT's Crucible 4-26 is testing links among sensors, command-and-control nodes and effectors across nations. The announcement identifies integration questions but provides no comparative battlefield-effectiveness results.
items.attribution: NATO Allied Command Transformation — official October 16 report

items.streamTitle: China's technology-policy network expanded without losing reported cohesion
items.streamSummary: Network analysis of 1,010 jointly issued policies found agency participation grew from 8 to 73 while reported cohesion remained high. Mission shifts correlated with restructuring; causation was not established.
items.attribution: Zhang, Chang and Chen — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: Compact multimodal models made typed decisions in one forward pass
items.streamSummary: Intern-Decision reported 90.02% average accuracy across seven suites and about 44 ms latency on one specified 4B-model test. Separate calibration and routing pilots were encouraging but limited.
items.attribution: Zhu et al. — arXiv preprint (Intern-Decision)

items.streamTitle: Simple agent-control rules improved some benchmarks but not all
items.streamSummary: A preprint found that reporting difficulties and scripted resets helped general agents in game-like evaluations; effects on Terminal-Bench were mixed and costs increased. Procedure design remained important.
items.attribution: Rodionov — arXiv preprint (EnvTraverse)

items.streamTitle: Trained AI auditors uncovered more policy violations during tool use
items.streamSummary: The PROBE preprint trained agents to test policy compliance through realistic multi-turn tool interactions and reported broader violation discovery than zero-shot probes. External deployment performance is unproven.
items.attribution: Mishra et al. — arXiv preprint (PROBE)

items.streamTitle: Real-time manipulation disclosures reduced belief shifts in AI conversations
items.streamSummary: A preprint experiment with 488 participants found 78% less belief shift toward a manipulative chatbot's goal when an interface exposed tactics and incentives. Real-world detection and long-term protection are not established.
items.attribution: Smith et al. — arXiv preprint (DISARM)

items.streamTitle: People assigned racial identities to AI without visual identity cues
items.streamSummary: Across five primary and eight supplementary studies, participants frequently perceived cue-free AI as White. Experimental changes to described training data also changed task assignments, though trust relationships were largely correlational.
items.attribution: Gamez-Djokic and Waytz — Journal of Personality and Social Psychology (newly highlighted October 16)

items.streamTitle: Ontology-enhanced drug-slang surveillance proposed, not tested
items.streamSummary: Researchers proposed pairing dynamic drug ontologies and retrieval with language models to detect coded online terms. The paper offers no implementation or validation results.
items.attribution: Valdez et al. — npj Digital Public Health (Perspective)

items.streamTitle: Teachers described cultural intelligence as context-dependent practice
items.streamSummary: Interviews with 16 trainee teachers linked multilingual teaching choices to reflection, cultural knowledge and institutional constraints. The study identifies experiences, not causal effects on learning.
items.attribution: Eliyahu-Levi and Gvura — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: Image-text agreement improved fake-news benchmark classification
items.streamSummary: COOLANT++ coupled shared image-text prototypes with confidence-based weighting and reported 90.0% and 92.3% accuracy on two datasets. Generalization and field reliability remain untested.
items.attribution: She, Ab Hamid and Hanif — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: Mindfulness did not increase preference for immediate rewards
items.streamSummary: Three experiments and an eight-week course study found no meaningful shift toward immediate monetary rewards. The informative null finding has limits outside the tested decisions and samples.
items.attribution: Gisbert et al. — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: Pentagon described path toward an Autonomous Warfare Command
items.streamSummary: Officials linked Project Agincourt and new Army structures to plans for scaling unmanned systems. Announced organization and deployments do not demonstrate improved combat outcomes.
items.attribution: U.S. Army / Pentagon News — October 15 official report

items.streamTitle: Dendrite-inspired AI reported efficient very-long-context memory
items.streamSummary: A neuroscience-inspired architecture linked simplified dendritic computations to attention and reported strong long-context benchmarks. Biological equivalence and deployment performance remain unproven.
items.attribution: Yao et al. — Nature Communications

items.streamTitle: Earthquake shelter model counted usable housing, not just deliveries
items.streamSummary: A Wenchuan-based logistics simulation explicitly modeled road disruption and shelter setup delays. Coverage fell under disrupted routes, with no feasible plan under severe conditions; field outcomes were not tested.
items.attribution: Zhang and Wang — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: War narratives revealed differences that symptom scores missed
items.streamSummary: A Lebanese observational study found non-linear differences in resilience and narrative expression across prewar, postwar and displaced groups. Selection and timing limit causal interpretation.
items.attribution: Fares et al. — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: NATO is making reversible, conditions-based changes to KFOR
items.streamSummary: NATO described a new KFOR commander and gradual peacekeeping posture adjustments in Kosovo. Its stability assessment and planned adjustments are not proof of operational effect.
items.attribution: NATO — October 15 official mission update

items.streamTitle: Causal-design review finds mostly favorable green-space health results
items.streamSummary: A review found 30 of 33 empirical studies using quasi-experimental methods reported at least one positive health association interpreted causally. Assumptions and bias still matter.
items.attribution: Ying et al. — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (Systematic Review)
